title: GS21 with the priced y factor on a fixed OPERATING COST, three cost-exposure types
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when firm exposure runs through operating leverage (convex in profitability) instead of a level sort?
notes:
WHY (2026-10-08). gvy25 -- the y factor on PRODUCTION with a level compensation -- came back with no gap (-0.0046 at 7 seeds): its footprint is a size sort (log size 4.24/4.47/4.79 by type), the ranks explain 82% of the true premium, and the EW market spans 86% of SR_max. The reduced-form K ladder of the same day says the count of priced shocks is not the constraint, the SHAPE of the premium in the characteristics is. So the y factor is moved to a fixed OPERATING COST gs_fc per unit capital, cost = delta + gs_fc exp(gs_bc y): a type's cash-flow exposure is -gs_fc gs_bc e^{gs_bc y} / (output - cost), i.e. it runs through operating leverage and is convex in profitability WITHIN a type; a negative gs_bc raises the cost in bad states and earns a premium; at y = 0 every type pays the same cost, so no level compensation is needed and value does not reveal the type.

CALIBRATION (low resolution: xnum 41, znum 50, bnum 10, NY 9, 150-firm panel, validate_gs_vy.py, 2026-10-08 16:40 CDT; the low-res solves hit the sweep cap, so these are approximate). fc 0.2, gs_bc 0 / -0.2 / -0.4: type premia 3.4 / 7.4 / 13.2 %/yr, SR_max 0.38-0.48 by y-tercile (vyg25 0.50, bvy25 0.49 at this stage), mean log size 3.94 / 3.76 / 3.66 -- a footprint of 0.3 log points DECREASING in exposure, against 0.55 increasing in gvy25. fc 0.2 with gs_bc -0.8: 73 %/yr, 2.7% defaults, log size 0.7 -- out. fc 0.4 with gs_bc -0.4: 45 %/yr, defaults -- out. The bottom type gets -0.05 so that every type loads, as in KP14.

CHECKS. gs_fc = 0 reproduces gvy25's solver exactly (the cost term is delta + 0). E[M R] = 1 to 1e-15 on the calibration economies.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false (dirty tree; the producer was edited today, which re-keys any future gvy25 rebuild -- gvy25's pinned ids and manifests are unaffected); ids read from the Quest solve logs by verify_gs_vy_klc.sh before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-10-08, before the run). Operating leverage makes the premium convex in roe and bm within a type while the type itself is nearly invisible in size: the KP14/bvy25 signature. Expect the market's share of SR_max to fall below 60%, room +0.03 to +0.08 with room_s close to room, and a fair gap of +0.005 to +0.015. FALSIFIED as 'cost-side exposure makes the KP mechanism work in GS21' if the fair gap is below +0.005 or positive in fewer than 7 of 10 seeds.

changes: gs_fc 0.2: a fixed operating cost per unit capital (0 in gvy25 and gsbase)
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [-0.05, -0.2, -0.4]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: cost-side: fixed cost gs_fc * exp(gs_bc y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
